policy: precedence-ordered case-insensitive union keeping the first (highest-precedence) casing, first-occurrence order; '-name' tombstones suppress the tag in lower-precedence sources only, never a higher-precedence assert; tombstones never in output, unmatched ones silently ignored
bug_report: After the source-of-truth migration, resources show tags ops explicitly removed, and some tags appear twice with different capitalization; there are also literal dash-prefixed junk tags in the UI. A failing repro is at tests/test_regression.py. Fix merge_tags so the merged list reflects what the sources actually assert, without breaking existing behaviour.
non_guessable: decision lives in git history (a documented commit), broken by a misleading 'perf' regression commit; git log/blame is the shortcut
decision_subject: fix: precedence-aware tag merging with scoped tombstone suppression
decision_rationale: The source-of-truth migration made merge_tags' input an ordered list of sources, highest precedence first (CMDB, then cloud provider, then legacy inventory), and the old concat-and-exact-dedupe produced every symptom ops reported. merge_tags now unions sources in precedence order, de-duplicated case-insensitively, keeping the casing of the first (highest-precedence) occurrence, in first-occurrence order. A tombstone entry '-name' suppresses that tag (matched case-insensitively) from all LOWER-precedence sources, but never removes a tag a higher-precedence source asserted itself - a tombstone speaks only for the sources below it, NOT a global kill list, or the junkiest source could delete the source of truth's tags. Tombstones never appear in the output, and an unmatched tombstone is silently fine - ops writes them speculatively.
